title: Unequal current noise removes a fixed time-average information bound in symmetric passive circuits
abstract: We tested whether unequal independent current noise preserves an earlier time-average information guarantee in symmetric passive circuits. For stationary constant input, known noise and full continuous observation, we prove a retained fraction of at least 0.877692222679276 divided by the noise covariance condition number. Commuting noise and decay matrices retain the earlier bound. A fixed two-cell circuit has a retained fraction that tends to zero as noise at the stimulated cell tends to zero. In two partial adult worm electrical maps, fourfold diagonal noise patterns gave point-input fractions below the earlier bound. At coupling scale 1, the minimum fractions on a fixed duration grid were 0.868899 and 0.870168 for high-degree noise, and 0.858704 and 0.865320 for a fixed random pattern. Direct covariance integration, Lyapunov solutions and sampled-path calculations checked the formulas. These are model results. No neural activity was measured, and the noise patterns were not fitted. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and an external retrieval recipe support reproduction.

display.caption: Unequal noise lowers time-average information retention in two partial worm-map models and a fixed two-cell model. All curves use assumed circuit and noise parameters.
